A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hydrodynamical approach is a very powerful tool to describe the dynamics of the early, dense and hot stage of the reaction, while the microscopic approach is essential to describe the hadronic stage of the reaction.
we have developed a new, fully three-dimensional, non-equilibrium, microscopic model, which can describe the space-time evolution of hot, dense, bulk QCD-matter.
we have shown that a combined hydrodynamics + microscopic transport approach is capable of describing the bulk of the data on transverse flow, elliptic flow and hadron production at RHIC.

we can explain all of the experimental data with a simple scenario of a fast thermalization of the bulk matter and subsequent hadronic expansion.
